I think the problem is around having two instances of PlayerNotificationManager registering a broadcast receiver. You should try using a single PlayerNotificationManager only.

I'd also suggest to have only a single player instance for all fragments in the ViewPager. 

That's a similar arrangement like for a RecyclerView. If you are using more than one instance of the player, you need to make sure that a given device has enough codec instances. This is not trivial because there's no reliable API to check the number of available codec instances.

If you choose to use more than a single ExoPlayer instance I'd still use only one instance of the PlayerNotificationManager and then use playerNotificationManager.setPlayer(player) with the player instance which is currently playing and for which you want to have a notification displayed.

But to make things easy, I'd go with one single player instance and one single PlayerNotificationManager instance and reuse these in the fragments. This also saves you from the problem to make sure that you've never two notifications displayed which may happen when you have two player instance/two notification manager at once.
I'll do a refactor and let you know how it turns out.

@marcbaechinger - I think all those suggestions are good, and have other important benefits. But as a separate point, I'm not sure I understand why this doesn't work correctly, and I wonder whether we could fix it regardless?

Intuitively I think I'd expect all registered receivers to get a broadcast triggered from any notification. Which would not result in correct behavior, but could possibly be fixed by putting an extra identifier into the intents, or something along those lines. That said, what I think I'd expect doesn't sound consistent with the described behavior. So... What does actually happen? And do you think it's fixable as a task that's independent from whether designing an app in this way is a good idea or not :)?
@ojw28 I'll create a test fixture with multiple PlayerNotificationManager's to see what happens.

I'm not sure what actually happens in the application of @aromanelli. However, in my test ficture I found the following behaviour:

I created two sets of a SimpleExoPlayer, a PlayerView and a PlayerNotificationManager with the same notification channel but a different NOTIFICATION_ID. This results in two notifications are shown in the notification drawer. When using the buttons in the notification, only the buttons of the second notification send an action, but these are sent to both broadcast receivers.

To fix that behaviour, we need to prefix (or suffix) the names of the actions for each player notification to make sure the actions are only delivered to the broadcast receiver which belongs to the given PlayerNotificationManager. This prefixing must be applied to all actions and also the custom actions of the CustomActionProvider to have everything kept separated nicely.

@marcbaechinger Concerning your last comment.  You've hit upon the issue I'm having, where the buttons in the notification only work for earlier instantiated/displayed fragments, and not later.  You could do fast flipping through fragments/pages, and get a fragment whose notification buttons would not work before, to start working, sometimes.

Also, please be aware, that if you use different NOTIFICATION_ID values, you'll have multiple notifications icons displayed, one for each fragment, even though only one fragment is visible, and the others are hidden (instantiated by ViewPager, but not displayed yet).  I would expect that only one notification icon/message would display, for the one that is actually visible in the ViewPager.

> Also, please be aware, that if you use different NOTIFICATION_ID values, you'll have multiple notifications icons displayed, one for each fragment, even though only one fragment is visible, and the others are hidden (instantiated by ViewPager, but not displayed yet). I would expect that only one notification icon/message would display, for the one that is actually visible in the ViewPager.

This doesn't sound like the responsibility of the ExoPlayer library. I don't think we have any way of telling what's visible or not in your application UI. Whereas your application code does, and so ultimately is responsible for managing any necessary lifecycles accordingly.

I would expect that only one notification icon/message would display, for the one that is actually visible in the ViewPager.

> This doesn't sound like the responsibility of the ExoPlayer library. I don't think we have any way of telling what's visible or not in your application UI. Whereas your application code does, and so ultimately is responsible for managing any necessary lifecycles accordingly.

Well, I was making that assumption because the way the ViewPager/adapter works is pre-instantiating fragments/pages before they are visible, so if I want to have each fragment have its own notification id/icon, it doesn't seem like its possible.  I was hoping that a simple "is visible?" check inside the library could handle if the notification should be displayed or not.  I'm coming from JavaFX/Java-Swing, where its easy to do a 'isVisible()' type of call, so I'm assuming Android has that same kind of functionality.

If you look at my code that I submitted for this bug, I tried doing manually managing the notifications so only the one that should be shown, is shown, and its allot of code that seems brittle/problematic (though to be fair, I am new to Android programming).  I ended up going with a single notification id just for the reason you mentioned, to help cut down on the 'management' coding needed.

Otherwise, you put allot of the responsibility on the developer to manage the state of the views, when the library is already managing the notifications on its own, and when a simple visibility check in the library would seem to be able to handle the same situation more cleanly, IMHO.  I would urge a solution along those lines, if possible.  If Android lacks that api (blows my mind if it does lack), then I'd understand not implementing that.

I think you're assuming components are more tightly coupled than they are, and making assumptions about how notifications should work that don't necessarily apply to other use cases. ExoPlayer as a library knows nothing about your ViewPager/Adapter. There's no real requirement that the player is bound to any view in the view hierarchy for a notification to be shown by `PlayerNotificationManager`, and even if there were, in many cases it wouldn't make sense to link the notification's visibility to the visibility of a corresponding view. Conversely, one of the primary uses of a playback notification would explicitly be to still allow control of the player when it's _not_ visible elsewhere in the UI.

It's your application code's responsibility to define the behavior you want and link things together. It should be reasonably easy for you to work out which views are visible in your app's UI, even within a ViewPager (I found a bunch of related StackOverflow questions and blog posts with a quick search). You do of course need to write some code to do this, and put some logic in place to achieve whatever behavior's you want, but that's kind of necessary given different apps will want different behaviors.
